column4: Use of non-private data in an easy (for automated tools) to process format by businesses, NPOs or other administrations than the administration publishing the data, in practical tools, services, visualisations or analyses

column7:
Sharing of cadastral parcel plan + statistics and police / emergency zones on  as open data (as opposed to a closed data source) reduces the administrative burden for municipalities and other administrations needing this data https://finance.belgium.be/en/experts-partners/open-data-patrimony/datasets/download-portal)

Same for portals like the Datavindplaats of the Flemish Region which also focuses on reuse by other administrations (https://www.vlaanderen.be/digitaal-vlaanderen/nieuwsberichten/eerste-versie-datavindplaats-gelanceerd), and the Brussels Region (https://datastore.brussels/web/)

column7:
Monthly overview of expenses by federal government (https://bosa.belgium.be/fr/budget-de-letat) provides transparancy on spending of tax payer's money, similar initiative in Brussels Region on public procurement expenses(https://openbudgets.be.brussels/en/data-table/table-1), Flanders Region (see also press article https://www.knack.be/nieuws/belgie/politiek/subsidieregister-laat-zien-dat-het-tijd-is-voor-een-kerntakendebat/) and in Walloon Region (https://subventions.wallonie.be/home.html)

Draft legislation of parliament (federal and regional) is sometimes used on social media for discussion

column7: "Provincies in cijfers" (provinces in numbers) provides data to help identify issues in municipalities (e.g. high unemployment rate or high number of vacant shops compared to average). https://provincies.incijfers.be/databank allows to dynamically compare several key indicators and to generate thematic reports (see also https://provincies.incijfers.be/dashboard/dashboard/ )  for e.g. city planners, community councils

column2: 4.3b Social impact

column4: There is data on social challenges, eg part of SDG indicators (gender equality, risk of poverty...) https://indicators.be/en/t/SDG/, though hard to say what the impact of open data is on these challenges
column7: The Flemish Provinces use the open data dashboard on SDGs to track progress of municipalities in achieving these goals, see also https://cdn.flxml.eu/m-7e0dddf44851770ee2dd728bc7106997da4f071c55402b3d, and to create the "Kansarmoede Atlas" (see https://kansarmoede.west-vlaanderen.be/gwportal/apps/sites/#/kansarmoede-atlas) and reports to create awareness on gender inequality in pensions (e.g. https://www.plan.be/uploaded/documents/202404250919410.REP_PensionGenderCapsEU_Report2_13001.pdf)

column7: Initiatives like https://www.onwheelsapp.com/nl/app/ (using OpenStreetMap open geo data) to check and document the accessibility of buildings. There is also data on social challenges, eg part of SDG indicators (gender equality, risk of poverty...) https://indicators.be/en/t/SDG/, though hard to say what the impact of open data is on these challenges

column7: While there is open data available on housing prices and number of sales etc (https://statbel.fgov.be/en/themes/housing/house-price-index), it's hard to tell what the impact is. The Flanders Region does have a use case on the reuse of open data by real estate agents, e.g. https://www.vlaanderen.be/datavindplaats/inspiratie/realsmart

column7: E.g. crowd-soruced air quality monitoring in Flanders like e.g. https://www.samenvoorzuiverelucht.eu (see also Dutch newsletter https://www.vmm.be/nieuwsbrief/september-2023/samen-met-lokale-besturen-en-burgers-naar-een-betere-luchtkwaliteit ), the "Internet of Waters" project ( https://www.internetofwater.be/en ) , and in Walloon Region the "open data for water and energy" workshop https://ecosysteme-economiecirculaire.wallonie.be/en/events/open-data-forwater-and-energy-use-cases-and-workshop/

column7:
Companies like AnyWays are using open data to offer better mobility services to companies and public administrations to reduce travel time and promote greener options https://www.anyways.eu/blog/2022-09-14-gipod

Regions also provide locations of public charging stations as open data to promote the switch from ICE to EV (https://www.vlaanderen.be/lokale-besturen-en-publieke-laadinfrastructuur)

Walloon Region has the "Wallonie-en-poche" apps which combines various open data sources into 1 app for citizens, e.g. for finding bike-sharing services https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7Svvcnr_WQI
